Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th president of the United States, is American nationalist, business nationalist, Christian libertarian, right-wing populist, and since 2015, ultraconservative. Trump has variously described himself as "common sense" and nationalist. Prior to 2016, he identified with the Democratic Party at times. Trump's political beliefs and ideologies are described as Trumpism.

Trump consistently advocates for supply-side economics, deregulation, energy independence, reindustrialization, school choice, "law and order" in law enforcement, and opposes illegal immigration. He also advocates isolationism, emphasizing a unilateral defense policy over collective security commitments, strengthened diplomatic and security relations with Israel, a protectionist trade policy, and strategic competition with China. He has also been accused of espousing racist and misogynist views.

Trump has personally cited Roy Cohn, Arthur Laffer, and Norman Vincent Peale as influences on his worldview. Jerome Corsi, Lee Iacocca, and Roger Stone are further purported to be influences on his politics.
